assumptions: The filing entity's membership in the circular's licensed-firm categories requires a separate assessment and is not inferred from platform use.
The specific launch and resumption provisions qualify the general effective-date wording for the post-launch assessment.
The selected event is an actual STR submission to the JFIU; registration, a technical test, direct contact and automatic record migration are separate event classifications.
Each assessed event has an identifiable submission method. Evidence from separate attempts or resubmissions is not combined to make one event satisfy the selected conditions.
Footnote 3 applies to the XML and prescribed-PDF alternatives carrying its marker. No certificate requirement for the web-based alternative is inferred from this footnote.

The source establishes a submission-related e-Cert requirement but does not establish that certificate availability alone satisfies it. Signing, authentication, attachment, certificate-holder identity and validity mechanics are not assumed.

The proposed decision concerns only the selected reporting channel, listed method and footnote 3 condition. It does not establish XML-schema conformity, completion of technical testing, reporting timeliness, substantive STR adequacy or overall legal compliance.

The blackout urgent-contact instruction and footnote 2 resubmission requirement remain separate. Resubmission does not change the original event's channel or time, and the retained text supplies no resubmission deadline.

citations.quote: licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual asset service providers and associated entities (collectively referred to as “licensed firms”)
With effect from 2 February 2026, STREAMS 2 will become the only channel for filing STRs2. Licensed firms are required to submit STRs to the JFIU via STREAMS 2 by one of the following means:
submission of an STR in an Extensible Markup Language (XML) format3;
uploading a completed STR form in the prescribed PDF format3; or
completing the web-based STR form in STREAMS 2.
Hongkong Post e-Cert (electronic certificate) is required for this submission.
the JFIU will cease accepting STR submissions via STREAMS at 12:00am on 28 January 2026, and will resume accepting STR submissions at 9:00am on 2 February 2026 via STREAMS 2
for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;
upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026, the operation of STREAMS will be discontinued. All STRs previously submitted through STREAMS will be migrated to STREAMS 2.

licensed firms that intend to submit STRs via the XML format are required to follow the XML schema provided separately by the JFIU and liaise with it as soon as possible to arrange a technical test to ensure a smooth transition.

For STRs submitted to the JFIU via channels other than STREAMS 2 following its implementation, licensed firms are required to re-submit the STRs via STREAMS 2. The JFIU will provide guidance to facilitate the re-submission.

original.distinction: The prior models already identify the relevant actors, distinguish channel from method, preserve the launch boundary and separate submission, contact, migration and resubmission events. The consequential remaining defect is the certificate relationship. Model abstraction.c8a341a59885fb7db63017bf makes certificate availability sufficient under an explicit assumption. Model abstraction.ebfcf1c1217258fc2b8613f9 instead requires supply or use 'in the manner required', but the required manner remains unspecified. The retained footnote supports a requirement for the particular submission; it does not resolve availability versus the operational act needed to satisfy that requirement. This proposal therefore withholds a complete compliance formula pending that information. It does not invent a rival signing, attachment or authentication requirement. Splitting the PDF components also prevents the file's format from concealing an incomplete form or a missing upload.
questions: What evidence establishes the submitting entity's classification within the circular's licensed-firm categories?
What is the assessed event's timestamp, and which timezone governs the stated launch and blackout times?
Was this an actual STR submission to the JFIU, and which channel and method did this particular event use?
For a PDF event, which prescribed form applied, was it completed, and was that completed form uploaded?
What operational relationship between a Hongkong Post e-Cert and an XML or PDF submission satisfies footnote 3, and what evidence establishes that relationship for this event?
Do the applicable technical requirements impose certificate-holder, authorization or validity conditions, and if so, what are they?
What do the separately provided XML schema and technical-test instructions require?
If the STR required urgent submission during the blackout, what direct contact with the JFIU occurred through a listed method?
Does the same STR have any actual post-implementation submission outside STREAMS 2, and what subsequent resubmission and JFIU guidance are evidenced?
original.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] The proposed question is whether one in-scope post-launch STR submission satisfies the selected STREAMS 2 channel, listed submission-method and footnote 3 conditions. True would mean that the event used STREAMS 2 and completed one listed method, including the submission-related Hongkong Post e-Cert requirement where XML or PDF was used. False would mean that at least one applicable selected condition failed. Neither an unknown fact nor an unknown or false scope produces a compliance verdict. Formalization is null because the retained source does not specify the certificate relationship needed to interpret the XML and PDF branches without substituting an unsupported operational assumption or an opaque satisfaction fact. No event-level truth value is assigned. This proposed meaning confers no legal approval.
original.subject: Submission-specific e-Cert requirement without substituting availability or an undefined satisfaction predicate

assumptions: The selected control is evaluated only for a classified licensed firm and an actual STR filing.
Unknown facts remain unknown rather than being treated as false.
Footnote 3 attaches to the XML and prescribed-PDF items because those items carry the marker; the web-form item does not carry it.

citations.quote: Licensed firms are required to submit STRs to the JFIU via STREAMS 2 by one of the following means:
upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026
For STRs submitted to the JFIU via channels other than STREAMS 2 following its implementation

original.distinction: Operational-launch reading: “following its implementation” begins at the explicit 9:00am STREAMS 2 launch. An off-channel STR filed at or after that time triggers the separate resubmission obligation. The strongest uncertainty is that footnote 2 does not expressly define implementation by reference to the launch time.

Does an urgent contact made before launch later require resubmission, and by when?

assumptions: The expressly timed transition provisions qualify application of the general calendar-date channel provision during the blackout.

citations.quote: the JFIU will cease accepting STR submissions via STREAMS at 12:00am on 28 January 2026, and will resume accepting STR submissions at 9:00am on 2 February 2026 via STREAMS 2
for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;

original.distinction: Urgent blackout contact is a separate transitional instruction. Treating it as a post-launch alternative filing channel, or treating contact as completed filing, would add an outcome the text does not state.
questions: What establishes urgency, and what procedure follows direct contact?
Are reports contacted about during the blackout later subject to an express filing or resubmission instruction?
original.statement: For STRs requiring urgent submission during the stated blackout, the text directs contact with the JFIU by the listed email, phone or fax. This includes the pre-launch hours of 2 February 2026. The packet does not establish whether contact itself completes submission; exact timestamp boundaries and that outcome are not formalized.
original.subject: Blackout urgent-contact exception

assumptions: The specific blackout arrangements qualify application of the general calendar-date channel statement.
Direct contact is not treated as proof that JFIU accepted a completed STR.

citations.quote: will cease accepting STR submissions via STREAMS at 12:00am on 28 January 2026, and will resume accepting STR submissions at 9:00am on 2 February 2026 via STREAMS 2
for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;

original.distinction: An urgent matter at 8:30am on 2 February remains within the blackout contact arrangement; one at 9:30am falls within the post-launch channel control. Applying the channel rule from midnight without preserving the contact arrangement would disregard the express blackout endpoint.
questions: What makes an STR require urgent submission?
What steps beyond direct contact complete urgent reporting during blackout?
original.statement: The selected blackout arrangement directs licensed firms with STRs requiring urgent submission to contact JFIU by the listed means until 9:00am on 2 February 2026. The source does not specify a complete filing procedure or establish that contact itself constitutes submission.
original.subject: Urgent blackout contact exception

assumptions: Intending to submit via XML is the stated trigger, which can arise before an actual filing.
Arranging a technical test is distinct from proving that a test has passed.

citations.quote: licensed firms that intend to submit STRs via the XML format are required to follow the XML schema provided separately by the JFIU and liaise with it as soon as possible to arrange a technical test to ensure a smooth transition.

original.distinction: Choosing a permitted XML format under the selected filing control does not exhaust XML-specific duties. The text requires schema conformity and prompt liaison, but does not expressly make successful test completion a filing prerequisite.
questions: What schema version applies?
How is as soon as possible assessed, and does separate guidance impose a test-passing prerequisite?
original.statement: Licensed firms intending to submit XML STRs must follow the separately provided JFIU schema and liaise with the JFIU as soon as possible to arrange a technical test. Missing schema contents and the contextual timing standard prevent a complete executable determination here.
original.subject: XML schema and technical-test liaison dependencies

assumptions: Following implementation is provisionally read against the expressly stated launch time.
The obligation is assessed separately from the initial channel control.

citations.quote: For STRs submitted to the JFIU via channels other than STREAMS 2 following its implementation, licensed firms are required to re-submit the STRs via STREAMS 2.
The JFIU will provide guidance to facilitate the re-submission.
All STRs previously submitted through STREAMS will be migrated to STREAMS 2.

original.distinction: The text imposes a corrective duty after an off-channel submission; it does not say that later resubmission retroactively satisfies the initial channel requirement. Automatic migration of previous STREAMS records is a different arrangement.
questions: When must resubmission occur, and what evidence links it to the original STR?
Does the promised guidance address blackout contacts?
original.statement: A licensed firm that submits an STR to the JFIU through another channel following implementation must separately re-submit that STR through STREAMS 2. No completion deadline or retrospective cure of the original channel failure is specified.
original.subject: Separate off-channel resubmission obligation

assumptions: The blackout begins at 12:00am on 28 January 2026 and ends when submissions resume at 9:00am on 2 February 2026.
The urgent-contact direction retains its please wording under the transitional should provision.
Pre-launch blackout contact is not treated as a post-implementation filing.

citations.quote: Licensed firms should observe the JFIU’s transitional arrangements as set out below:
the JFIU will cease accepting STR submissions via STREAMS at 12:00am on 28 January 2026, and will resume accepting STR submissions at 9:00am on 2 February 2026 via STREAMS 2
for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;

original.distinction: The blackout arrangement attaches to urgency during a bounded interval, not to urgency at any time. It therefore does not supply a continuing post-launch exception. A hypothesis that every listed contact method completes filing or automatically triggers footnote 2 lacks support. The source does not settle follow-up for blackout-only submissions.
questions: What constitutes completed urgent filing through the blackout arrangements, and what later follow-up is required?
original.statement: For an STR requiring urgent submission during the blackout, licensed firms are directed to contact JFIU through a listed email, phone or fax method. This instruction remains separate from the post-launch channel control and does not establish that contact alone completes filing.
original.subject: Urgent blackout contact and its limited attachment

assumptions: The offer is assessed as one indivisible package.
The package is treated according to its dominant or principal economic character, if such a character can be established.

citations.quote: distributors should not offer any gifts (other than a discount of fees or charges)
as they may be considered a gift that should not be offered to investors.

original.distinction: A competing reading treats the exception as applying to the combined package when its principal character is a fee or charge discount. The supplied text does not provide a dominance or inseparability test, so this reading is materially less supported and cannot be operationalised without additional authority.
questions: Does the referenced FAQ or full Code specify how bundled or inseparable benefits are classified?
Can the package be decomposed economically and contractually?
original.statement: The source leaves unresolved whether a genuinely inseparable package containing a discount and another benefit is assessed component-by-component or as a whole package.
original.subject: Alternative attachment of the fee/charge discount exception
